title: Lighten CI agent, generate toolchain lease, and minimize presubmit weight
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Reduced presubmit latency by ~30% via lighter CI agent bootstrap and toolchain leasing. Added capability to hold short-lived toolchain leases to avoid repeated full bootstraps; routing rules for low-risk PRs introduced. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation:
We observed spikes in presubmit queue latency caused by expensive agent bootstrap and toolchain installation on ephemeral runners. This patch makes two complementary changes: (1) introduce a short-lived 'toolchain lease' that lets CI runners reuse prepared toolchains for a configurable window, and (2) shrink and optimize the CI agent bootstrap so cold-start overhead is minimized. Together these changes target ENG-3184 and ENG-3220 and are intended to reduce presubmit wall-clock time without changing test coverage.

What this PR does (high-level):
- CI agent: factor out heavy startup phases (image verification, full manifest expansion) into a fastpath that runs concurrently with a lightweight health probe. The agent now favors a cached toolchain when a valid lease exists.
- Toolchain lease: add a lease allocator service and local lease file (.ci/toolchain-lease.json) so subsequent jobs on the same runner can reuse validated toolchains for a TTL (configurable; default 15m).
- Presubmit routing: introduce a small fastpath in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml that directs low-risk changes (docs, examples, ci-config only) to a slim job that skips heavy integration shards.
- Observability: add metrics for lease hits/misses and agent bootstrap time, exported to Prometheus and surfaced in Console.

Commits (summary):
- Add minimal toolchain lease allocator and lease file handling (lease.go + allocator tests)
- Refactor agent bootstrap to use lease and add fastpath probe (agent.go + bootstrap tests)
- Update presubmit workflow to include fastpath routing and lightweight job profile (presubmit.yml)
- Small docker image tweaks: compress toolchain layers and remove unused buildtools (ci/Dockerfile)
- Telemetry and metrics: expose ci_toolchain_lease_hits and agent_bootstrap_seconds counters
- Tests and docs: unit tests for lease expiry and short integration smoke for presubmit fastpath; docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md

Files/areas changed (high level):
- scripts/ci/agent.go (refactor bootstrap path, add lease lookup)
- scripts/ci/lease.go (new: allocator and local lease file handling)
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (fastpath job + tagging rules)
- ci/Dockerfile (shrink image, remove python wheels we no longer use)
- build/toolchains/manifest.json (lease TTL default added)
- docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md (design + operational runbook)
- monitoring/prometheus/ci.rules (new metrics)
- test/ci/lease_test.go (unit coverage)
- test/ci/presubmit_smoke.sh (integration shim)

Testing and CI:
- CI run summary: unit -> pass, integration-smoke -> pass (one flaky matrix shard retried once), lint -> pass. The full presubmit matrix was exercised in the staging lane; we measured median bootstrap reduction ~28% on our staging runners.
- Performance numbers (staging): median agent bootstrap from 65s -> 47s; toolchain install frequency down 45% on consecutive jobs within TTL window.

Review conversation highlights:
- Diego: "Can we make TTL configurable per-queue? For long-running release lanes we'd want a shorter TTL to avoid stale toolchain drift."
- Author (Aisha): "Yes — manifest.json includes default TTL; I've added queue-level override support and documented it in docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md. We can add policy to L4 if we see drift."
- Lin: "Agent logs on lease miss look noisy; can we reduce INFO level noise and surface distinct lease miss metric?"
- Author: "Addressed — reduced log level to DEBUG for expected misses and added ci_toolchain_lease_misses counter. Also added a short backoff before re-install to avoid thundering-herd on lease expiry."
- Priya: "Pipeline safety: what happens if lease file becomes corrupted on disk?"
- Author: "Agent will treat corrupted lease as miss and recover; added defensive parsing and a documented cleanup script. Also added unit test covering corrupted lease file."

Edge cases and known limitations:
- This change improves hot-runner cases; ephemeral single-job runners (e.g., cloud-hosted ephemeral VMs that don't share filesystem) get limited benefit. We added a feature flag to gate lease allocator per-runner pool.
- Toolchain drift: leases are short by default and require owner to bump manifest when toolchain changes. Ops runbook includes steps to revoke leases cluster-wide if needed.

Rollout plan and safety:
- Feature gated behind ci.featureFlags.toolchainLease (default on for internal staging pools, off for external ephemeral pools).
- Gradual rollout: start internal staging -> dev runners -> all presubmit lanes over 72 hours while monitoring lease_hit_ratio and agent_bootstrap_seconds.
- Fallback: if regressions observed, feature flag can be toggled off and a small re-image of runners will clear stale toolchains.

Related work and links:
- Linear: ENG-3184 (toolchain leasing experiment), ENG-3220 (presubmit latency reduction)
- Design doc: docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md
- Small follow-ups expected: add per-repo leases, and consider shared network-attached cache for fully ephemeral pools.

Merge outcome:
- All reviewers approved; CI green; merged via squash on 2026-02-22. Post-merge: deployment of allocator to staging on 2026-02-23, monitored for 48 hours with no regressions.

Checklist (from PR template):
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Docs updated (runbook + design)
- [x] Feature flagged for gradual rollout
- [x] Metrics added

If you're reviewing this after merge and want to poke at the runtime telemetry, the new metrics prefix is ci_toolchain_lease_* and agent_bootstrap_seconds is histo-bucketed for SLO tracking. For operational questions see docs/ci/toolchain-lease.md or ping @aisha on Linear ENG-3184.
notes: Staging rollout monitored; no incidents. Follow-ups: per-repo lease, network cache exploration.
footprint: Adds small lease service (~600 LOC), minor Docker image shrink (~40MB), and CI workflow changes to accelerate presubmit feedback loops.
